fullPassage: [Analysis] Water essentially has no persona of its own, but has an extraordinary quality. Water as a liquid has no shape, yet it is readily defined by its surroundings. Water has no hardness; it is completely yielding to the touch, yet is hard as concrete when impacted at high speed. Water has no color when viewed in a transparent container, yet becomes vividly green or blue as an ocean, and readily reflects at its surface everything around it. Pure water has no taste, yet it readily absorbs and transmits the taste of any suspended or dissolved substances. It has no smell, yet, as atmospheric humidity, readily distributes the aromas of its surroundings. This ubiquitous part of our environment truly has a variable personality, readily changing to assimilate its surroundings. [Passage 1] I suppose everyone has at one time or another drawn a mental map, and it offers little conceptual difficulty. In my classes, I ask students to draw a map by hand, in just five minutes, showing their route to and from class. No two maps are ever entirely the same, of course, and none are to scale. Nevertheless, most of the maps are easily understood. This shows that while we all produce our own versions of spatial reality, we can see particular landmarks that communicate to all of us in a social community. Mental maps tend to highlight important parts of a route, with streets labeled to indicate where to turn. Such maps tend to include informal but understood cultural references. Where a professionally made street map might give you numbered addresses, a mental map is more likely to describe a route by referencing visible features like "a giant blue gorilla" outside a car dealership or "that old pink Victorian house." [Passage 2] People tend to pay less attention to familiar things, whether it's a possession or even a person. On the whole, this adaptive behavior is biologically useful (for objects, events, and situations), because it is usually the novel, unexpected things in life that require the most attention. The brain naturally adapts to repeated experiences. If I were to show you a series of repeated images and measure your brain responses, the activity would diminish with the repetitions. Your brain would respond again only when something new was presented. Scientists have shown that the biggest responses always come with the least expected event. A simple sentence such as, "He picked up the hammer and nail" gives a tiny response; change the last few words, "He picked up the hammer and ate it," and you'll see a much larger one. [Passage 3] In one experiment, Keith Markman and two colleagues gave participants ten anagrams to solve. After supposedly "grading" the results, they told participants that they'd found only half of the available words. Then they poked people with a little regret. "Close your eyes and think about your actual performance on the anagrams compared to how you might have performed better," they told the participants. "Take a minute and vividly evaluate your performance in comparison to how you might have performed better." Their heads now swimming with If Onlys, these puzzle-solvers felt worse — especially compared to another group that had been asked to make At Least comparisons. But on the next round, the regretful group solved more puzzles and stuck with the task longer than anyone else in the experiment. This is one of the central findings on regret: it can deepen persistence, which almost always elevates performance.

questions.passage: [Analysis] Water essentially has no persona of its own, but has an extraordinary quality. Water as a liquid has no shape, yet it is readily defined by its surroundings. Water has no hardness; it is completely yielding to the touch, yet is hard as concrete when impacted at high speed. Water has no color when viewed in a transparent container, yet becomes vividly green or blue as an ocean, and readily reflects at its surface everything around it. Pure water has no taste, yet it readily absorbs and transmits the taste of any suspended or <u>dissolved</u> substances. It has no smell, yet, as atmospheric humidity, readily distributes the aromas of its surroundings. This ubiquitous part of our environment truly has a variable personality, readily changing to assimilate its surroundings.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 dissolved와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① melted: 녹은. dissolved(용해된)와 가장 유사한 의미 ←정답
❌ ② frozen: 얼어붙은. dissolved의 반의어 방향
❌ ③ hardened: 굳어진. dissolved와 반대 방향의 변화
❌ ④ evaporated: 증발된. 상태 변화이나 용해와는 다른 개념
det.tip: dissolved substances = 용해된 물질 → melted(녹은)가 가장 유사

questions.passage: [Passage 2] People tend to pay less attention to familiar things, whether it's a possession or even a person. On the whole, this adaptive behavior is biologically useful (for objects, events, and situations), because it is usually the <u>novel</u>, unexpected things in life that require the most attention. The brain naturally adapts to repeated experiences. If I were to show you a series of repeated images and measure your brain responses, the activity would diminish with the repetitions. Your brain would respond again only when something new was presented. Scientists have shown that the biggest responses always come with the least expected event. A simple sentence such as, "He picked up the hammer and nail" gives a tiny response; change the last few words, "He picked up the hammer and ate it," and you'll see a much larger one.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 novel과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① familiar: 익숙한. novel의 반의어
❌ ② repeated: 반복된. 본문에서 novel과 대비되는 개념
✅ ③ new: 새로운. novel(참신한/새로운)과 가장 유사한 의미 ←정답
❌ ④ expected: 예상된. unexpected와 함께 쓰인 novel의 맥락에 반대
det.tip: the novel, unexpected things — novel = new, 소설이 아닌 '참신한/새로운'의 형용사 의미

questions.passage: [Passage 3] In one experiment, Keith Markman and two colleagues gave participants ten anagrams to solve. After supposedly "grading" the results, they told participants that they'd found only half of the available words. Then they poked people with a little regret. "Close your eyes and think about your actual performance on the anagrams compared to how you might have performed better," they told the participants. "Take a minute and <u>vividly</u> evaluate your performance in comparison to how you might have performed better." Their heads now swimming with If Onlys, these puzzle-solvers felt worse — especially compared to another group that had been asked to make At Least comparisons. But on the next round, the regretful group solved more puzzles and stuck with the task longer than anyone else in the experiment. This is one of the central findings on regret: it can deepen persistence, which almost always elevates performance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 vividly와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① briefly: 간략하게. 생생하게와 반대 방향
✅ ② graphically: 생생하게/선명하게. vividly와 가장 유사한 의미 ←정답
❌ ③ casually: 대충, 무심하게. 생생하게와 반대 방향
❌ ④ reluctantly: 마지못해. 태도를 나타내는 말로 선명함과 무관
det.tip: vividly evaluate = 생생하게 평가하다 → graphically(생생하게/선명하게)가 가장 유사

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 absorbs와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① releases: 방출하다. absorbs(흡수하다)의 정반대 동작 ←정답
❌ ② soaks up: 빨아들이다. absorbs의 동의어
❌ ③ retains: 보유하다. 흡수 후 유지하는 것으로 유사 방향
❌ ④ collects: 모으다. 흡수와 유사한 방향
det.tip: absorbs(흡수하다) ↔ releases(방출하다) — 물이 맛을 흡수하는 맥락

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 diminish와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① decrease: 줄어들다. diminish의 동의어
❌ ② fade: 사라지다. 감소와 유사한 방향
❌ ③ shrink: 줄어들다. diminish의 동의어
✅ ④ amplify: 증폭하다/확대하다. diminish(줄어들다)의 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: diminish(줄어들다) ↔ amplify(증폭하다) — 뇌 활동이 반복으로 줄어드는 맥락

questions.passage:
(A) Water as a liquid has no shape, yet it is readily <u>defined</u> by its surroundings.
(B) The researcher clearly <u>defined</u> the scope of the experiment before collecting data.
questions.stem: 다음 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 defined의 의미로 가장 적절한 것을 각각 고르시오.

det.korean: (A) defined = 형태가 결정된/규정된, (B) defined = 정의한/명확히 한
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 제한된 — (B) 정의한: (A)는 제한보다는 형태가 결정되는 맥락
✅ ② (A) 형태가 결정된 — (B) 명확히 규정한: 물이 주변에 의해 형태가 결정되고, 연구자가 범위를 명확히 규정한 맥락에 정확히 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ (A) 형태가 결정된 — (B) 묘사한: (B) defined는 묘사보다는 규정/정의의 맥락
❌ ④ (A) 명확히 규정한 — (B) 형태가 결정된: (A)와 (B)의 의미가 뒤바뀜
det.tip: defined by surroundings = 주변에 의해 형태 결정 / defined the scope = 범위를 명확히 규정

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to continue firmly in a course of action in spite of difficulty or opposition"

det.korean: 어려움이나 반대에도 불구하고 행동 방침을 단호히 계속하다 = persist(고집하다/끈질기게 하다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① abandon: 포기하다. 계속하는 것과 반대
❌ ② surrender: 항복하다. 어려움에 굴복하는 것으로 반대
✅ ③ persist: 고집하다/끈질기게 계속하다. 정의와 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ retreat: 후퇴하다. 어려움에서 물러나는 것으로 반대
det.tip: persist = continue firmly despite difficulty. 3번 지문의 persistence(끈기)와 연결되는 핵심 어휘

questions.passage: This shows that while we all produce our own versions of spatial reality, we can see particular landmarks that communicate to all of us in a social _____. (commune)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어의 알맞은 형태를 쓰시오. (영어로) (commune)

det.analysis: commune(공동체/동사: 교감하다) → community(명사: 공동체). social 뒤에 명사가 필요하며, 사회적 공동체(social community)가 문맥상 적절
det.tip: in a social community — commune의 명사형 community

questions.passage: On the whole, this adaptive behavior is _____ useful (for objects, events, and situations), because it is usually the novel, unexpected things in life that require the most attention. (biology)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어의 알맞은 형태를 쓰시오. (영어로) (biology)

det.analysis: biology(명사: 생물학) → biologically(부사: 생물학적으로). useful(형용사)을 수식하므로 부사 형태가 필요
det.tip: biologically useful — biology의 부사형. 명사→형용사(biological)→부사(biologically)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸=assimilate(동화시키다). 물은 주변 환경을 동화시키며 변하는 가변적 성격을 지님
det.analysis:
❌ ① reject: 거부하다. 주변 환경에 맞춰 변한다는 맥락에 부적절
❌ ② resist: 저항하다. 물이 주변에 적응하는 것과 반대
❌ ③ escape: 벗어나다. 물이 환경에서 벗어난다는 맥락이 아님
✅ ④ assimilate: 동화시키다. 물이 주변 환경을 받아들여 변하는 핵심 특성 ←정답
det.tip: readily changing to assimilate its surroundings — 물의 가변적 성격의 핵심은 주변 동화

det.korean: 빈칸=deepen persistence(끈기를 깊게 하다). 후회가 끈기를 강화하여 성과를 높인다는 결론
det.analysis:
✅ ① deepen persistence: 끈기를 깊게 하다. 후회한 그룹이 더 오래 과제에 매달리고 더 많이 풀었다는 실험 결과와 일치 ←정답
❌ ② weaken motivation: 동기를 약화시키다. 후회가 오히려 성과를 높인다는 맥락에 부적절
❌ ③ eliminate effort: 노력을 제거하다. 후회가 더 많은 노력으로 이어지는 실험 결과에 부적절
❌ ④ reduce performance: 성과를 줄이다. elevates performance와 모순
det.tip: regret can deepen persistence → elevates performance — 후회의 긍정적 효과: 끈기 강화 → 성과 향상
